note: Adapted from the original English description by Constantino (1990) (new genus and new species, type locality Serra do Navio, Amapá, Brazil, collected on 2 November 1989 (month 11) by R. Constantino, MPEG 3267; the specific epithet from the MacArthur Foundation, which funded the study). The genus-level characters are translated as well, because the genus is monotypic; the alate is unknown. Measurements in millimetres.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Genus level: soldier head capsule wide and rounded, the nasus conical-cylindrical, long and slender; distinguishable from the other Neotropical soil-feeding nasute genera by the very wide head and the long, slender nasus; labrum short, not visible in dorsal view; reduced mandibles without apical points; antennae 13-segmented, extending slightly beyond the apex of the nasus; pronotum about half as wide as the head; head almost hairless, with only a few setae on the vertex and hairs at the apex of the nasus; tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Worker mandibles and gut similar to those of Cyranotermes, differing in the smaller molar prominence with the molar tooth points exposed, the cutting edge of the first and second marginal teeth concave (undulate in this genus), the third marginal tooth larger, and the right mandible without a trace of the second marginal tooth.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Capsule and postmentum orange; nasus iron-orange, deepening towards the apex; antennae and pronotum orange-yellow, the sclerites semi-transparent, pale yellow. Head with 2 setae (on the vertex); hairs at the apex of the nasus. Pronotum, mesonotum and metanotum without setae. Legs with a few setae. Tergites with 4 long setae on the posterior margin; sternites with a row of long setae on the posterior margin and scattered short setae on the surface. Antennal segment 3 longer than segments 2, 4 and 5, segments 2 and 4 about equal in length, segment 5 longer than segment 4. Measurements (mm; 5 individuals): head length including nasus 2.33—2.40; nasus length 1.15—1.22; head width 1.27—1.32; head height (excluding the postmentum) 0.80—0.85; pronotum width 0.63—0.66; hind tibia length 1.11—1.22; maximum width of the postmentum 0.36—0.38.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head, antennae and legs pale yellow; pronotum yellowish white; sclerites semi-transparent, pale yellow. Head capsule with a row of 4 setae at the middle and 2 posteriorly; postclypeus with 6 setae; labrum with 8 setae. Pronotum with long setae at the margins. Tergites and sternites with a row of long setae on the posterior margin; sternites with many short setae on the surface; legs with many long and short setae. Antennal segment 2 longer than segments 3, 4 and 5, segments 3 and 4 about equal in length, segment 5 longer than segment 4. Worker monomorphic; head capsule rounded, widest in the anterior part; postclypeus moderately arched; antennae 14-segmented; apical tooth of the mandibles well developed, the inner margin concave; left mandible with the cutting edge of the first and second marginal teeth undulate, the third marginal tooth small, the molar tooth points hidden below the molar prominence, the molar prominence large and rounded, without ridges; right mandible with the third marginal tooth reduced and almost absent, the molar plate concave. Abdomen swollen, the sclerites and membrane transparent, the gut contents visible. Gut: crop enlarged, asymmetrical; gizzard with a sclerotized armature, without spines; mixed segment present, shorter than the width of the midgut; Malpighian tubules inserted as in figure 11; first proctodeal segment shorter than the midgut; enteric valve ventrolateral, the armature with 3 longitudinal primary ridges alternating with 3 longitudinal secondary ridges, the large spines arranged in an arc, the small spines scattered; colon long. Biology: a single colony collected in unstructured soft soil beneath a fallen decaying tree trunk in primary rain forest; a soil and humus feeder, probably subterranean; soldiers and workers move slowly.
